title: Genesis Bible Quiz - Chapter 21
description: Ten questions on Genesis 21: the birth of Isaac, Hagar and Ishmael sent away, and Abraham's covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba.

questions.text: How old was Abraham when his son Isaac was born?
questions.explanation: Abraham was one hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

questions.text: What did Sarah say after Isaac was born?
questions.explanation: Sarah said, "God has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me."

questions.text: On which day did Abraham make a great feast for Isaac?
questions.explanation: The child grew and was weaned, and Abraham made a great feast on the day that Isaac was weaned.

questions.text: What did Sarah see the son of Hagar the Egyptian doing?
questions.explanation: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.

questions.text: What did Abraham give Hagar when he sent her away?
questions.explanation: Abraham rose early, took bread and a container of water, put it on Hagar's shoulder, gave her the child and sent her away.

answers.text: A bag of silver and gold
Bread and a container of water
Sheep and cattle from his flock

questions.text: What did Hagar see when God opened her eyes?
questions.explanation: God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She filled the container and gave the boy a drink.

questions.text: What did the boy become as he grew up in the wilderness?
questions.explanation: God was with the boy, and he grew. He lived in the wilderness, and as he grew up, became an archer.

questions.text: From which land did Hagar get a wife for her son?
questions.explanation: He lived in the wilderness of Paran, and his mother got a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.

questions.text: What did Abraham set apart as a witness that he had dug the well?
questions.explanation: Abraham set seven ewe lambs by themselves and told Abimelech to take them as a witness that he had dug the well.

questions.text: What did Abraham plant in Beersheba?
questions.explanation: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and called there on the name of Yahweh, the Everlasting God.
